+#+title: The barrier direction belongs on the lookup table
+#+description: The FX barrier check names the Up and Down styles beside the lookup that holds them. A style added to ores_trading_barrier_types_tbl falls into the no-direction branch, so the check and the table can disagree with no signal. Encode the direction on the lookup row and let the check read it.

 * Decisions
 
+- *A closed vocabulary is stated in its lookup table, not in a check.* Five FX
+  vocabularies were stated twice. The foreign key now validates the code, so the
+  check is the copy that was removed; the lookup is what a reader edits and what
+  the store enforces.
+- *An exercise style admits the whole ORE set.* The vanilla option's check
+  refused Bermudan while its prose and the lookup both admitted it. The check
+  goes with the other duplicates, so the set is the lookup's: European, Bermudan
+  and American.
+- *A single barrier's level sits in the column its direction names.* An Up style
+  or a cap engages the upper level, a Down style or a floor the lower one, and
+  the other column stays null. The columns were positional, so an UpAndOut
+  option could not be stated without inventing a lower level.
+- *A product that states two levels is the exception, and its trade type says
+  so.* The directional check names FxBarrierOption alone; the double and generic
+  barriers hold a level per side, and a double barrier must state both.
+- *The digital option requires what each code engages and tolerates the rest.*
+  The one synthetic generator fills a strike and both barriers on its single
+  row, so a check that refused another code's field would refuse that row.
+
 - The family was reviewed on 2026-10-16, and the review is recorded as [[id:38931409-479B-40C3-A118-16D234C687C9][Investigation: FX family data model review]]. It found that the per-type tables already meet the explicit-variation check, so a family header and per-product fact tables are not required by the checklist.
 - The units below carry the deviations the review found. If the header and the fact tables are still wanted for another reason, record that reason here and add the acceptance it serves.
 - The units run digits first, because that unit moves the goldens.

 * Result
+
+* Findings
+
+- *The economic-digest suite is rotted, and not by this unit.* No CMakeLists
+  adds =projects/ores.trading/core/digest_tests=, so the suite is outside the
+  build. Wiring it in and running it fails four cases, one of them for
+  =ScriptedTrade=, a family this unit never touches, because the digest column
+  is empty before and after the write. The suite was therefore left unwired and
+  is recorded as its own defect.
+- *The wire twins and the goldens are corrected here.* Both TS files now type
+  the lower level as =string | null=, and the barrier golden records the level
+  in =upper_barrier= with a note that says so.
+- *The direction is a second list.* The check names the Up and Down styles
+  beside the lookup that holds them. Encoding the direction on
+  =ores_trading_barrier_types_tbl= is the right shape and is captured as its
+  own work.
+
+The duplicated vocabularies are gone. Ten =in (...)= checks named a set the
+lookup table now validates, so the checks were the second copy and are removed.
+The vanilla option's check was one of them, which settles the exercise style:
+the lookup holds European, Bermudan and American, so the store admits all three
+and the prose states that set once instead of contradicting it.
+
+The barrier option now states which level its style engages. A single
+=FxBarrierOption= with an Up style or a cap holds its level in =upper_barrier=
+and leaves =lower_barrier= null; a Down style or a floor does the reverse; the
+styles that name no direction state one of the two. =lower_barrier= became
+nullable for that reason, and the mapper places the document's level by
+direction instead of by position, so an UpAndOut option no longer needs a lower
+level invented for it. A double or generic barrier holds a level per side and
+is exempt, because its trade type says so.
+
+The digital option keys its checks on the trade type. Each of its four codes
+states the fields it engages: a plain digital a strike, a touch one barrier, a
+double touch both barriers, and a digital barrier a strike and a barrier. The
+checks require those fields and tolerate another code's, because the one synthetic
+generator fills a strike and both barriers on its single row, so a check that
+refused a field the code does not engage would refuse that row.
+
+The decisions are in the parent story's =* Decisions=.

+/**
+ * @brief Whether a barrier style names the direction it engages.
+ *
+ * An Up style or a FixingCap engages the upper level, a Down style or a
+ * FixingFloor the lower one. The styles that name no direction keep the level
+ * in the lower column, which is the shape their readers expect.
+ */
+bool is_up_barrier_style(const std::string& type) {
+    return type == "UpAndOut" || type == "UpAndIn" || type == "FixingCap";
+}
+

+TEST_CASE("an_up_style_refuses_a_lower_level", tags) {
+    auto lg(make_logger(test_suite));
+
+    database_helper h;
+    const auto party_id = boost::uuids::random_generator()();
+    auto ctx = h.context().with_party(h.tenant_id(), party_id, {party_id}, h.db_user());
+
+    // An Up style engages the upper level, so a row that also fills the lower
+    // level states a shape the product cannot hold.
+    auto instr = make_instrument(h);
+    instr.lower_barrier = ores::utility::decimal::decimal::from_string("1.1").value();
+
+    // The refusal names a check constraint, so a different failure cannot pass.
+    fx_barrier_option_instrument_repository repo;
+    try {
+        repo.write(ctx, instr);
+        FAIL("the store accepted an Up style with a lower level");
+    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
+        CHECK(std::string(e.what()).find("violates check constraint") != std::string::npos);
+    }
+}
